note: Developer/API module. It adds ONE plugin to Simple OAuth's Oauth2Grant plugin type: id 'password' (Drupal\simple_oauth_password_grant\Plugin\Oauth2Grant\Password), wrapping the PHP League PasswordGrant. There is no settings page (configure=null), no permissions, no Drush. The grant is turned on per Consumer entity via its multi-value grant_types field (value 'password'); a client then POSTs grant_type=password + client_id/client_secret/username/password to Simple OAuth's /oauth/token. Credential checks (username OR email, active users only) and flood protection live in service simple_oauth_password_grant.repositories.user. Easy cases probe that surface as text. Medium/hard cases are grounded in Consumer config the agent can create WITHOUT any live token exchange: enabling the password grant in a consumer's grant_types, verified against the consumer entity. Consumers are namespaced with sopg_* client_ids.

evals.prompt: I enabled simple_oauth_password_grant on a decoupled Drupal 11 site. How does a trusted first-party client obtain an OAuth2 access token using a Drupal user's credentials? Give the grant_type value and the parameters to POST.
evals.expected_output: POST to Simple OAuth's token endpoint (/oauth/token) with grant_type=password plus client_id, client_secret, username and password. The username may be the Drupal username or the account email. You first enable the Password grant on the consumer. Response returns an access_token (and refresh_token when allowed).

evals.prompt: There is no admin settings page for simple_oauth_password_grant. On a Simple OAuth Consumer, where/how do I turn the password grant on?
evals.expected_output: Enable the 'Password' grant on the specific Consumer entity by adding 'password' to its grant_types field (Configuration > Web services > Consumers, tick Password). configure is null; there is no module settings form.

evals.prompt: With the simple_oauth_password_grant password grant, can a user authenticate with their email address instead of their Drupal username, and what protects the token endpoint against brute-force login attempts?
evals.expected_output: Yes - the username field accepts the Drupal username or the account email (email matched first when it contains @). The module's UserRepository applies core flood protection using user.flood limits (IP event oauth2_password_grant.failed_login_ip and per-user oauth2_password_grant.failed_login_user), throwing a 403 flood_ip_blocked / flood_user_blocked when exceeded.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a Simple OAuth Consumer labelled 'SOPG Probe Consumer'. Inspect the live consumer configuration and state whether the OAuth2 password grant is enabled on it.
evals.expected_output: Yes - the consumer (client_id sopg_probe_client) has grant_types including 'password' (and 'refresh_token').

evals.prompt: On this site exactly one Simple OAuth Consumer has the password grant enabled. Inspect the live consumers and report that consumer's client_id.
evals.expected_output: The consumer with grant_types containing 'password' has client_id sopg_probe_client (label 'SOPG Probe Consumer').

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a Simple OAuth Consumer with client_id 'sopg_task_client' that does NOT currently allow the password grant. Enable the OAuth2 password grant on that consumer and save it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: The consumer with client_id sopg_task_client has 'password' added to its grant_types field (value saved on the consumer entity).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create a Simple OAuth Consumer with client_id 'sopg_new_client' that has the OAuth2 password grant enabled, and save it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A consumer entity with client_id sopg_new_client exists and its grant_types field includes 'password'.
